analysis:
The only change in this PR is a single documentation row added at docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 572. It documents a `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode with `--prompt-prep-lengths` and `--iterations`. The mode is described as CPU only, loading only the tokenizer, timing prompt preparation and body decode for chat, agent and tool-loop conversations, printing JSON, and exiting 2 on any token-ID or decoded-field difference. The rest of the file in both units is unchanged context. It includes the logout, revocation, drain, doctor, models and cache-location text, and I did not treat any of that as changed.

Security relevance: no code, auth, attestation, encryption or coordinator contract changes are visible in this diff. The row references provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift, which is not supplied. Whether the benchmark generates synthetic prompts or could read real consumer content (A-001), log it, or write it to disk is therefore unverified. The documented output is timings and token-ID differences. The row says nothing about a coordinator connection, so I identified no new trust-boundary crossing. The text also reads as a developer harness, not a serving path, so it should not touch T-041 cache behavior, T-053 or TB-011 authorization. The row does not mention prefix-cache interaction. This remains a documentation claim only.

Remaining question for integration: confirm that the actual benchmark source, if added in other units, uses only synthetic inputs and does not persist or print real prompt text. If no such source is in this PR, no further review is needed.
